subject: Post-call: Data jurisdiction & retention clarifications
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@harborhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Data jurisdiction & retention clarifications

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and the asks we promised to follow up on from the call: 

1) Scope of PII and data types
- You mentioned PHI-lite (patient identifiers + appointment metadata) and clinical notes may be uploaded by users. Please confirm whether any of your integrations will send unredacted SSNs or national IDs.

2) Default logs & retention
- Current Redwood default: streaming logs + request/response traces stored for 30 days, audit logs 365 days (configurable). We can propose a 30-day default for request logs and offer shorter retention for sensitive routes. Need to confirm what your procurement / privacy team will accept.

3) Data residency & failover tolerance
- We can pin production to a US-only footprint (single region) or US-primary with warm-standby in EU for DR. For the EU warm-standby option, we replicate encrypted snapshots across regions; failover would involve a brief DNS cutover and session replay limitations for KV cache. Please tell us your tolerance for cross-border backups (are backups allowed to be stored outside the US?).

4) Backups & key management
- Backups are encrypted at rest. We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). If you need HSM-backed keys and a specific KMS (e.g., AWS KMS with a restricted key policy), flag that.

Next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm whether backups may be geo-replicated outside the US and provide any required retention windows for logs/audits.
- Us: provide a short matrix showing defaults vs. options (pin to US, US-primary with EU warm-standby, EU-only).
- Deliverables: updated DPA snippet for regional controls + SOC2 summary + a draft mutual action plan for procurement.

I've attached our SOC2 summary and will draft the regional controls language for the DPA. Olga will propose how we implement pinning and snapshot cadence.

Thanks — I’ll hold on sending a formal options matrix until we hear your cross-border stance.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0132

From: Alice Park <alice@harborhealth.com>

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Data jurisdiction & retention clarifications

Thanks Rishi — good recap. A couple of clarifications from our security team (see infra-sec CC):

- We do not plan to send SSNs. However, clinical notes can include patient identifiers (MRN, DOB).
- For production data, procurement prefers backups remain within the US. For non-prod/test datasets we can permit cross-region replication.
- For logs: we require a 90-day window for audit trails related to billing events; request/response payloads may be configurable down to 7 days for controlled routes.

Could you provide a matrix that shows: default behavior, pin-to-US option, and US-primary-with-EU-warm-standby (specifically whether backups or snapshots would be replicated to EU in that option). Also: do you redact PII from model inputs before storing logs (automatic redaction) or do you rely on customer-supplied redaction?

Attaching our security questionnaire (partial) so you can see the level of detail infra will want: harbor_security_questionnaire.pdf

We can schedule a short follow-up (30 min) with Infra next week to go over the matrix. Proposed times: Wed 11/18 10:00 or Thu 11/19 14:00 EST.

Best,
Alice
Senior Product Manager, HarborHealth

Subject: RE: Post-call: Data jurisdiction & retention clarifications — suggested answers and next steps

Looping in suggested responses and a short plan for the follow-up with Infra. I drafted language for a DPA regional clause and a 3-row matrix for the options. Key points to propose to HarborHealth:

- PII redaction: Redwood supports optional automatic PII scrubbing for common identifiers (SSN, emails, credit card) at ingestion via a configurable filter. For clinical free-text we recommend customer-side tagging plus our scrubber; we can offer a managed service (paid) to run additional NLP redaction if they need it.

- Retention: Offer 7/30/90 day presets for request logs; default to 30 days for request/response payloads, 90 days for audit/billing trails (matches their ask). Allow contract-level override.

- Backup replication & pinning options:
  * US-only (pin): snapshots and backups remain in US regions only; no cross-border copies.
  * US-primary, EU warm-standby: encrypted snapshots replicated to EU but encrypted with CMK restricted by customer policy; data plane reads remain US unless failover initiated.
  * EU-only: we can offer EU-only control plane + data plane for enterprise (requires Private deployment).

- KMS: we can support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys; for HSM-backed keys, we will need procurement/legal to sign a KMS connectivity addendum.

Attachments: harbor_mbp_draft_v1.docx (mutual action plan draft), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Proposed next steps:
1) Send Alice the matrix + DPA snippet (I can redline).
2) Run the 30-min Infra call with Olga and Rishi to confirm backup replication tolerances.
3) If HarborHealth wants US-only pin, we prepare a procurement-ready offer with a 12-mo reserved capacity quote.

Rishi — please confirm availability for Wed 11/18 10:00 EST (Alice's preference). Olga — can you prepare a short slide that explains operational steps for pinning and snapshot cadence?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
